title: Among users located in the United Kingdom who have earned the 'Teacher' bad
question: Among users located in the United Kingdom who have earned the 'Teacher' badge, find those whose posts—authored under their account—have received more than 4 votes. Return the count of such distinct users.

prediction.sql:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT u.XCL_052) AS user_count
FROM users u
INNER JOIN badges b ON u.XCL_052 = b.XCL_002
INNER JOIN posts p ON u.XCL_052 = p.XCL_033
INNER JOIN (
    SELECT XCL_067 AS post_id
    FROM votes
    GROUP BY XCL_067
    HAVING COUNT(*) > 4
) v ON p.XCL_026 = v.post_id
WHERE u.XCL_058 = 'United Kingdom'
  AND b.XCL_003 = 'Teacher'

The submitted SQL correctly identifies users in the United Kingdom with the 'Teacher' badge who have authored at least one post with more than 4 votes, and counts the distinct users. The use of a derived table for the vote count ensures that the 'more than 4 votes' condition is applied per post before joining back to the user, preventing row multiplication from inflating the count (though COUNT DISTINCT handles this, the derived table is a clean way to express the post-level condition). The condition 'posts have received more than 4 votes' is correctly implemented as a post-level aggregate (GROUP BY votes.XCL_067 HAVING COUNT(*) > 4) in a derived table, which is then joined to the user's posts. This ensures that a user qualifies if they have *at least one* such post, without requiring all their posts to meet the threshold.

The final count uses COUNT(DISTINCT u.XCL_052), which correctly counts unique users even if a user has multiple qualifying posts or multiple 'Teacher' badges (though the latter is unlikely, the former is possible).
The join from users to posts (u.XCL_052 = p.XCL_033) correctly identifies posts authored by the user, as per the question's 'authored under their account' requirement.
